JSON Schema for the edits an agent may send

Source: R/ops.R
plan_ops_schema.Rd

Describes the operations form of edits (see build_scenario()) as a JSON Schema, draft 2020-12: an array of ops, each exactly one of the shapes the op constructors build. Hand it to a tool-calling model as the type of its edits argument, and a malformed op is refused before R sees it.

Usage

plan_ops_schema(plan = NULL, as_json = FALSE)

Arguments

plan

Optional MediaPlan to narrow the schema to.

as_json

FALSE (default) returns the schema as a nested list; TRUE returns it as JSON text.

Value

A nested list, or a json string when as_json = TRUE.

Details

Without a plan, the schema says what any op may look like. With one, it narrows to what is legal on that plan, which is the contract to give an agent working on it:

  • target may name only the plan's grain columns, each limited to the values present.

  • Dates take the shape the plan's time basis uses: YYYY-MM-DD for a plan keyed by day, week or month; a date or a date-time for a plan of moments.

  • add must name every line item column, and may set only columns the plan has.

The schema is the first check, not the only one. Some rules depend on the plan's rows in ways a schema cannot state – values that each exist but never occur together, a shift that would collide with a row already planned – and build_scenario() still enforces them.

To read an agent's ops in R, parse with jsonlite::fromJSON(x, simplifyVector = FALSE). Simplifying turns an array of ops into a data frame, which build_scenario() would read as an allocation rather than a list of operations.

See also

ops for the constructors that build each shape.

Examples

schema <- plan_ops_schema()
vapply(schema$items$oneOf, function(op) op$title, character(1))
#>  [1] "set"        "scale"      "delta"      "delta_each" "total"     
#>  [6] "transfer"   "add"        "drop"       "shift"      "restage"   
#> [11] "rebound"   

plan <- media_plan_from_df(
  data.frame(week = as.Date("2026-07-06"),
             channel = c("TV", "Search"), planned_spend = c(80, 40)),
  grain = "channel", time = "week", name = "base"
)
# On a plan, `target` lists the values an op may name.
scale <- plan_ops_schema(plan)$items$oneOf[[2]]
scale$properties$target$properties$channel
#> $anyOf
#> $anyOf[[1]]
#> $anyOf[[1]]$enum
#> [1] "Search" "TV"    
#> 
#> 
#> $anyOf[[2]]
#> $anyOf[[2]]$type
#> [1] "array"
#> 
#> $anyOf[[2]]$items
#> $anyOf[[2]]$items$enum
#> [1] "Search" "TV"    
#> 
#> 
#> $anyOf[[2]]$minItems
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> 
#> 

cat(substr(plan_ops_schema(plan, as_json = TRUE), 1, 200))
#> {
#>   "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
#>   "title": "mediaplanr edits",
#>   "description": "Edit operations applied in order to derive a scenario. Each op carries exactly one opera
